questions.q: From the top of a tower, a stone is thrown up and reaches the ground in time ${t}_{1} = 9s$. A second stone is thrown down with the same speed and reaches the ground in time ${t}_{2} = 4 s$. A third stone is released from rest and reaches the ground in time ${t}_{3}$, which is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $u$ be the initial upward velocity of the ball from $A$ (the top of the tower) and let $h$ be the height of the tower.

Taking the downward motion of the first stone from $A$ to the ground is positive, we have

$h = - u{t}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}^{2}$...(i)

Taking the downward motion of the second stone from $A$ to the ground is positive, we have

$h = u{t}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{2}^{2}$...(ii)

Multiplying Eq.(i) by ${t}_{2}$ and Eq. (ii) by ${t}_{1}$ and adding we get

$h\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}{t}_{2} ( {t}_{1} + {t}_{2} )$

So, $h = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}{t}_{2}$...(iii)

For stone falling under gravity from the top of the tower

$h = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{3}^{2}$...(iv)

From Eqs. (iii) and (iv), ${t}_{3}^{2} = {t}_{1}{t}_{2}$ or ${t}_{3} = \sqrt{{t}_{1}{t}_{2}}$

$= \sqrt{9 \times 4} = 6\text{s}$
